inspiration.observed_pattern: Two grouped customer queries use year-specific HAVING thresholds and INTERSECT to retain customers above the threshold in both years.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored service-order audit. Two grouped YEAR-based branches intersect accounts with at least three orders in each of two fixed years, while a conditional aggregate report independently exposes both yearly counts; the source tables, identifiers, dates, and customer-order context are new.

fixture_notes: Account 120 meets the threshold in both years; accounts 121 and 122 meet it in only one year; account 123 meets it in both with extra orders. The INTERSECT result must contain 120 and 123, while the conditional aggregate exposes all yearly counts.
determinism_notes: Account IDs and order dates are fixed. Set-operation and aggregate results are ordered by account ID, with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE service_orders (order_id INT PRIMARY KEY, account_id INT NOT NULL, ordered_on DATE NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT account_id FROM service_orders WHERE YEAR(ordered_on) = 2024 GROUP BY account_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 INTERSECT SELECT account_id FROM service_orders WHERE YEAR(ordered_on) = 2025 GROUP BY account_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY account_id

SELECT account_id, SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(ordered_on) = 2024 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_2024, SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(ordered_on) = 2025 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_2025 FROM service_orders GROUP BY account_id HAVING orders_2024 >= 3 AND orders_2025 >= 3 ORDER BY account_id

checks.sql: SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM service_orders GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY account_id
